description: Runs the monitor as SYSTEM. On a runner without UniFi Endpoint it must stay healthy by default, alert when alertIfMissing is on, and turn an out-of-range variable into a 'Check could not run' alert - each with exactly the documented exit code and a result block. Then it plants an uninstall entry and a fresh cached latest version (so the vendor is never asked) and proves an old version alerts and a current one, with an extra build number, is healthy.

steps.label: Not installed: healthy
outputContains: STATUS=UniFi Endpoint is not installed; nothing to check.

steps.label: Not installed with alertIfMissing: alert
outputContains: STATUS=UniFi Endpoint is not installed on this device (alertIfMissing is on).

steps.label: Out-of-range cacheHours: check could not run
Plant UniFi Endpoint 3.6.0.100 and a fresh cached latest of 3.7.4
steps.run:
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$key = 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\TCTestUniFiEndpoint'
New-Item -Path $key -Force | Out-Null
New-ItemProperty -Path $key -Name DisplayName -Value 'UniFi Endpoint' -Force | Out-Null
New-ItemProperty -Path $key -Name Publisher -Value 'Ubiquiti Inc.' -Force | Out-Null
New-ItemProperty -Path $key -Name DisplayVersion -Value '3.6.0.100' -Force | Out-Null
# A fresh cache answer, so the monitor does not ask the vendor
$dir = Join-Path $env:ProgramData '_automation\UniFiEndpoint'
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $dir | Out-Null
[pscustomobject]@{ Version = '3.7.4'; FirstSeenUtc = $null; LastSuccessUtc = [datetime]::UtcNow.ToString('o'); FirstFailureUtc = $null } |
    ConvertTo-Json | Set-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $dir 'latest.json') -Encoding UTF8
'planted 3.6.0.100'

steps.label: Installed and behind: alert, from the cache without asking the vendor
outputContains: STATUS=UniFi Endpoint 3.6.0.100 is behind the latest version 3.7.4.

steps.label: Plant UniFi Endpoint 3.7.4.301, the cached latest with a build number
